featured_reviews.name: Dhruv Vaghela
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐ 1/5 - Absolutely Disgusting Hygiene Conditions at Uttan BeachVisited: October 2025
I am extremely disappointed and disgusted with the current state of Uttan Beach. What should be a beautiful natural attraction has turned into a nightmare due to complete lack of basic sanitation facilities.
The most shocking issue: People are openly defecating right on the beach in public view. Yes, you read that correctly - individuals are sitting in open areas of the beach doing their business with zero regard for hygiene or public decency. This is absolutely unacceptable and revolting.
The beach desperately needs:Public toilets/restrooms - There are virtually no proper toilet facilities availableBetter monitoring and enforcement - Authorities need to patrol and prevent such unhygienic behaviorAwareness campaigns - Clear signage prohibiting such activities
Regular sanitation workers - Daily cleaning and maintenanceWhile beach cleanup drives have removed tons of garbage, the lack of basic toilet infrastructure is creating a major health hazard.
This is not just about cleanliness - it's a serious public health concern that can spread diseases and contaminate the beach water.
I cannot recommend visiting this beach until the municipal corporation takes immediate action to install proper sanitation facilities and enforce hygiene standards. Families with children should absolutely avoid this place in its current condition.
To MBMC authorities: Please wake up and address this crisis immediately. A beautiful beach is being ruined by lack of basic amenities.
यह बीच पूरी तरह से गंदा है। लोग खुले में शौच कर रहे हैं और कोई शौचालय की सुविधा नहीं है। बहुत शर्मनाक स्थिति है।

featured_reviews.name: Umesh Rane
featured_reviews.review_text:
The statue of Chimaji Appa near Dongri Fort in Uttan was built by the Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation in 2022 to honor a brave Maratha warrior. Chimaji Appa was the younger brother of Peshwa Bajirao I, and he is famous for winning the Vasai Fort from the Portuguese in 1739. During this mission, Dongri Fort was an important place that helped the Maratha army. Today, his statue stands near the fort, facing the sea, and is surrounded by a beautiful garden where people can relax and enjoy nature.
The area is part of a lively fishing village where the Koli community lives, adding a local cultural touch. Nearby, visitors can also explore quiet beaches, old churches, and small guesthouses. This place is becoming popular for tourists who love history, nature, and peaceful surroundings. Local people are working to protect this heritage and promote respectful tourism.

featured_reviews.name: Ronit Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had been looking for a good place to enjoy a Friendship Day lunch, and with a group of 15 friends, Pali Village turned out to be a great choice. The restaurant arranged a sort of private table for us, which made it feel special and comfortable for our large gathering. The ambiance has a nice rustic charm, and it felt like the perfect place to sit back, enjoy conversations, and share a hearty meal.

We began with soups – some of us chose the Cream of Tomato, while a few went for the Vegetable Manchow. The Cream of Tomato was spot on with its rich yet balanced sweetness, smooth consistency, a drizzle of cream, and crunchy breadcrumbs to top it off. It was satisfying and flavorful. However, the Manchow soup was a bit of a letdown – while it had plenty of veggies, it was extra spicy and lacked that signature tang and flavor one usually expects. Adding fried noodles made it slightly better, but overall it fell short compared to the tomato soup.

For starters, we tried a variety – cheese balls, honey chilli potatoes, stuffed mushroom tandoori, and peanut chaat. The cheese balls were the highlight, perhaps the best I’ve had, mainly because they were pure cheese without any fillers like corn. Each bite burst with soft, molten cheese wrapped in a crunchy outer layer – a real treat for cheese lovers. The honey chilli potatoes tasted good but were overwhelmingly spicy despite us asking for medium spice. The stuffed mushrooms were generously portioned and very well received – smoky from the tandoor, with a flavorful paneer and veggie filling. On the other hand, the peanut chaat didn’t quite work for us; it had a vinegar-like coating that felt unusual, making the dish more average than enjoyable.

Moving on to the main course, we ordered Malai Kofta, Paneer Butter Masala, and Veg Handi, along with a mix of rotis, naans, and makai roti. The Malai Kofta was outstanding – rich cashew gravy, creamy but not overly sweet, with soft, perfectly cooked koftas that paired wonderfully with the hot rotis. Both the Paneer Butter Masala and Veg Handi were excellent too. The paneer pieces were soft, with ample portions in the creamy orange gravy, and the dish was made exactly as per our request without coriander. The Veg Handi lived up to its name with a mix of beans, carrots, peas, and cauliflower, all cooked well and full of flavor. The breads were soft, served hot, and generously buttered – the perfect partner to the gravies.

We ended our lunch with a sizzling brownie topped with vanilla ice cream. Though a few desserts we wanted weren’t available, this one made up for it. The brownie was warm, soft, and rich in chocolate flavor, pairing beautifully with the cold vanilla ice cream. Overall, while a few dishes could improve, the experience at Pali Village was very good. The ambiance, service, and food made it memorable, and the place also has little corners for photos and even parakeets and rabbits that add to the charm. It’s a wonderful choice for family outings as well as large groups.

featured_reviews.name: Krutarth Malwankar

I had a wonderful experience. The ambiance is peaceful, resturant is well-designed with plenty of seating, and made even more enjoyable with great music playing in the background. It’s the kind of place where you instantly feel relaxed and happy.

The food was delicious and full of flavor, and the service staff was impressively quick and attentive, which made the overall experience even better.

There is also an attached hotel for overnight stays, along with a pool area, which we didn’t get a chance to explore this time but it looked very inviting. A lovely added bonus is the small fair area on the premises, with fun shooting games, a trampoline for kids, and a pool table for adults which is perfect for families and groups.

Overall, it’s a fantastic spot to enjoy great food, a lively yet calming atmosphere, and entertainment. We’ll definitely be visiting again!

P.S. no cats were intoxicated during the visit 🤣

It's serene around the talav but the roads outside are in a terrible shape causing too much traffic during school hours.

The storm water department has been working since last year on these roads and only making things worse every time they try something. Excessive fisherwomen make it disgusting throughout the day by throwing waste fish and the illegal vendors cause crowds on certain days.
